Answer: B
Reason: The CT images (Figures 1a-1c) demonstrate diffuse, randomly distributed micronodules throughout the lung parenchyma, which is the hallmark radiographic appearance of miliary tuberculosis. This finding correlates strongly with the clinical history of prolonged fever and elevated sedimentation rate, whereas the other options describe patterns (large nodules, peribronchovascular distribution, or single mass) not seen in the provided scans.
